promise: "We intend to designate this disaster as an 'Extremely Severe Disaster'" - all-out government support for Kumamoto earthquake recovery, including Cabinet reserve funds
description: Following Takaichi's August 3 remarks, the Cabinet approved JPY24.2 billion from contingency reserves on August 4, 2026. MAFF subsequently published a notice concerning designation of the Kumamoto earthquake as a disaster of extreme severity.
evidence: Cabinet approved 24.2bn yen in reserve-fund spending on Aug 4, 2026
Extremely severe disaster designation still being prepared as of Aug 5, 2026

review.note: Reserve allocation verified. MAFF subsequently published the designation-order notice, so an August 5 preparation snapshot is stale. Exact legal effective date and a promised August 31 cutoff require confirmation; not every recovery task is completed by designation.

promise: Present a national proposal to regulate cell phone and social media use in schools by the end of August 2026
description: On August 3, 2026, Sheinbaum set an objective of presenting a schools-focused proposal toward the end of August. Her administration subsequently announced an August 24-25 teacher consultation.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: retrieved official material confirms consultation but no dated publication of the promised national proposal.

role: Government of Hungary / EU Recovery and Resilience Facility
promise: Complete all milestones and targets required to unlock the full 10 billion euros in EU recovery funds by August 31, 2026
description: Hungary sought to complete reforms and investments for approximately EUR 10 billion of recovery funding by the EU's end-August deadline. The government said on August 31 that it had met the conditions.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the retrieved reporting records Hungary's self-assessment, not the Commission's final acceptance of every milestone.

review.note: The EU confirms the August 31 milestone deadline. A government claim of compliance is not Commission acceptance. The original August 13 promise date was not established; August 24 coverage alone cannot date the earlier commitment.

person: Femi Gbajabiamila (Presidential Working Group on State Police)
role: Chief of Staff to the President of Nigeria
promise: Extend public submissions on Nigeria's National Policing Bill until August 21, 2026 at 5 p.m. West Africa Time
description: Gbajabiamila's working group extended the public consultation window by eight days on August 13, 2026.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the retrieved reports announce the extension but do not document that the submission portal actually remained accessible through the cutoff; starting bill drafting does not establish fulfillment.
